key_insight: SAGE-PINN makes axisymmetric cylindrical flow PINNs stable by reparameterizing the radial coordinate and embedding conservation and boundary conditions into the network, removing the usual axis singularity.
engineering_relevance: This enables mesh-free simulation of coupled flow and heat-transfer problems in cylindrical geometries, such as stenosed arteries, without case-specific tuning.
method: Uses the parity-preserving variable s = r^2 to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms.
Employs a modified stream-function form so mass conservation is satisfied identically.
Adds boundary-fitted analytical ansätze, staged momentum-thermal joint training, residual normalization, and continuation in Péclet and Richardson numbers.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions for steady nanofluid flow and heat transfer, achieving single-precision mass conservation and central-range errors of about 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-driven slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
